newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Precious metals to consolidate after gain.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Precious metals to consolidate after gain.

text.p: SPOT NY CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
The precious metals are probably overcooked after the aggressive rallies of recent days and may need to consolidate before resuming the advance, analysts said.
Gold may ease to $345 an ounce or further in the near term, while silver could drop back to $4.75 and platinum towards $385.
GOLD - After zooming up from below $340 a week ago to above $350 on Monday, gold prices have eased back and are likely to move sideways for a while before rechallenging the upside.
"As per usual, gold isn't likely to sustain its initial move and a period of consolidation is looking overdue," said technical analyst Karen Jones of Credit Suisse First Boston.
Gold could drop back to $345 or even $343.50 without losing its sparkle on the charts, she added. On the upside, resistance will emerge in the $354-$355 area which capped the market in March.
The platinum-gold spread, which hit a recent high of 48 and has provided good underpinning for gold's gains, also looked overdone and could be due for a test of the 38-40 area.
But it showed potential to head up to 60, Jones said.
At 0745 GMT spot gold was indicated at $346.65/$347.15, compared to Monday's New York close of $347.40/$347.90.
SILVER - Having advanced just above $4.90 in recent days, silver has completed a 50 percent retracement of its last leg lower, and is also likely to consolidate around current levels, analysts said.
Support is expected in the $4.75 area, where the 10- and 30-day moving averages crossed on Monday.
Resistance is seen just above recent highs at $4.93, the level of the 200-day moving average.
At 0745 GMT spot silver was indicated unchanged at $4.82/$4.84.
PLATINUM - Prices were lower on Tuesday morning after surging towards the $400 mark on Monday, and the overdone market was expected to follow the same consolidation pattern as gold, Jones said.
On the charts, dips to $385 support were seen possible ahead of a resumption of the uptrend, with $400 offering initial psychological resistance.
Above that, tough barriers were seen at the year's high of $406 and a 10-year downtrend line at $410.
Traders said the market was still anxiously awaiting fresh news regarding Russian supplies.
At 0745 GMT spot platinum was indicated at $389.00/$390.00, compared to Monday's New York close of $392.35/$393.35.
--Lida Poletz, London newsroom +44 171 542 2936
